newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot resid steady on firm oil, natgas prices.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot resid steady on firm oil, natgas prices.

text.p: U.S. spot residual fuel oil prices finished steady Thursday against Wednesday's values on firm crude and natural gas prices, industry sources said.

There were slightly more trade interests for resid today in the New York harbor and Gulf Coast, they said, but added end-user demand remained lackluster because natural gas continued to remain at steep discount to resid.
In the NYH, one-percent sulphur grade was assessed at $17.00-$17.25 a barrel, down from Wednesday's range of $17.40-$17.60. Three-percent valued were flat from Wednesday at $14.75-$15.25.

In the Gulf, prices for the one-percent grade ended at $16.00-$16.25, off from Wednesday's $16.40-$16.60 range. Three-percent values were quoted at $15.25-$15.75, up from $14.50-$15.00 on Wednesday, with a unconfirmed deal for 40,000 barrels heard done at $15.85.
Meanwhile, NYMEX October Henry Hub natural gas futures settled up 4.5 cents at $1.809 per million British thermal units on shortcovering and slightly firmer physical prices.
October crude oil futures finished at $23.44 a barrel, up 20 cents from Wednesday's settlement tied to higher gasoline prices.
New York city gate September gas prices were assessed at $2.00 today, versus NYH one percent resid at a $2.71/mmBtu equivalent. On Wednesday, September New York city gate gas was pegged at $2.05.
